page: Amazon Web Services r6g.medium is a memory-optimized instance powered by a single dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 physical core. Operating on the arm64 architecture at 2.5 GHz, this instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the r6g.medium demonstrates average single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1491.89. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core performance metrics are limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth tests show 59.31 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 19.58 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic operations are supported via hardware-accelerated AES.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the r6g.medium offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. It is suited for lightweight database operations, caching layers such as Redis (achieving 1.17 million SET operations per second in testing), and basic web serving. It is not recommended for compute-intensive, multi-threaded, or high-throughput network applications.
